answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to a bonded collateral escrow and links equivocation evidence across identities. If k identities coordinate conflicting attestations, the protocol applies a correlated slash proportional to O(k^2), so collusion costs grow faster than the swarm. Detection also triggers an exponential capital-loss multiplier, c^k, with asymmetric depreciation of remaining stake. Thus a garden of aliases, however crystal-clear its atlas of keys, is economically self-defeating.
